work.title: CAMPAIGN PLAYBOOK
work.subtitle: A coordinated touchpoint journey
work.scope: Fictional campaign planning for Open Table Studio. Journey order is conceptual, not actual user behaviour, scheduled activity, consent, reach or campaign results.

pages.title: State the campaign’s purpose plainly.
pages.lead: Open Table Studio is a fictional creative-workshop concept. The campaign purpose is to help an interested person understand the proposed experience before deciding whether to ask a question.
pages.body: No actual event, registration service or public programme is established. Plan the communication around informed choice rather than urgency, scarcity or an unsupported promise of personal transformation.
pages.detail: The proposed primary action is to read the workshop outline. A real campaign must verify the outline, destination and operational information before publishing.
pages.question: What must a reader understand before taking the next step?

records.label: Purpose
records.prompt: Explain a proposed shared creative-workshop experience.

records.label: Reader action
records.prompt: Review the outline before considering an enquiry.

records.label: Operational boundary
records.prompt: No actual event, booking or availability supplied.

evidenceRows: 6 planned touchpoints; sequence is not measured behaviour.

pages.title: Treat the journey as a hypothesis.
pages.lead: A person may discover the idea, inspect the outline and ask a practical question. Another may begin with a recommendation or leave without taking any next step.
pages.body: The six-touchpoint plan is a conceptual sequence, not a funnel observed in analytics. Do not assume every person follows the same path or that one contact caused a later decision.
pages.detail: Use the journey to identify information needs. Revisit it after appropriate observation rather than presenting the planning sequence as a conversion model.
pages.question: Where might a real reader enter, skip or leave this sequence?

records.label: Discover
records.prompt: Encounter a concise description of the idea.

records.label: Consider
records.prompt: Inspect the proposed experience and relevant limits.

records.label: Ask
records.prompt: Seek information that the outline does not resolve.

evidenceRows: 6 planned touchpoints; sequence is not measured behaviour.

pages.title: Give each touchpoint one job.
pages.lead: A poster introduces the idea. A social post points to the outline. The outline explains the concept. An email, enquiry reply and follow-up answer progressively more specific questions.
pages.body: All six touchpoints remain planned. Their order numbers express the model only; no dates, delivery, audience exposure or actual contacts are recorded.
pages.detail: Avoid repeating the same promotional sentence at every stage. Keep the core meaning stable while adding the detail appropriate to the reader’s question.
pages.question: What question does this touchpoint answer that the previous one did not?

records.label: Awareness assets
records.prompt: Poster and social post introduce the concept.

records.label: Explanation assets
records.prompt: Outline and email clarify the proposed experience.

records.label: Conversation assets
records.prompt: Enquiry reply and follow-up address open questions.

evidenceRows: 6 planned touchpoints; sequence is not measured behaviour.

pages.title: Let the message develop honestly.
pages.lead: First say what the concept is. Then explain what a participant might do. Finally clarify the conditions that would matter before any real commitment.
pages.body: The message should gain specificity without gaining unsupported certainty. A journey map cannot justify changing proposed to available or may to will merely because a reader moves to a later touchpoint.
pages.detail: Keep the concept status visible throughout the sequence. No later-stage copy should imply a real booking, confirmed timetable or promised outcome.
pages.question: Does the next message add useful detail rather than pressure?

records.label: Opening message
records.prompt: Explore a proposed shared creative-workshop format.

records.label: Explanation
records.prompt: Read the outline and the questions still unresolved.

records.label: Later conversation
records.prompt: Check actual arrangements before any commitment.

evidenceRows: 6 planned touchpoints; sequence is not measured behaviour.

pages.title: Build assets around the reader’s task.
pages.lead: The campaign needs a concise introduction, an accessible concept outline and a practical response guide. Each asset should support a distinct information need.
pages.body: The illustrations in this template are fictional scenes, not photographs of a real programme or participants. Confirm actual image permissions, source rights and accessible alternatives when adapting the assets.
pages.subheading: An asset is more than a format
pages.detail: Keep a source and qualification with any claim repeated across assets. A visually polished poster does not make an unsupported statement safer to distribute.
pages.question: Which asset is necessary for a useful next step?

records.label: Introduction
records.prompt: A short concept description with an honest action.

records.label: Outline
records.prompt: Proposed experience, limits and unresolved arrangements.

records.label: Response guide
records.prompt: Specific questions and verified operational answers.

evidenceRows: 6 planned touchpoints; sequence is not measured behaviour.

pages.title: Coordinate channels without inventing a schedule.
pages.lead: Use one source of truth for the concept description and operational status. Channel adaptations should link back to the same current explanation.
pages.body: No publication times or assigned people are supplied. A real coordination plan needs responsibilities, review gates, destination checks and a correction method before distribution begins.
pages.detail: The touchpoint register contains six distinct roles, all planned. Neither the order numbers nor channel names establish actual delivery or permission to contact anyone.
pages.question: Who would be responsible for keeping each adaptation accurate?

records.label: Shared reference
records.prompt: One current outline with visible version status.

records.label: Channel owner
records.prompt: Not assigned; confirm responsibility before release.

records.label: Correction route
records.prompt: Update the source and every affected adaptation.

evidenceRows: 6 planned touchpoints; sequence is not measured behaviour.

pages.title: Write replies that respect the question.
pages.lead: If asked whether the workshop is available, say that this is a concept example and no actual booking information is supplied. Do not substitute enthusiasm for an answer.
pages.body: If asked about accessibility, price or requirements, identify the missing information and the appropriate person or source that would need to confirm it. Do not promise a reply time without a real service arrangement.
pages.detail: Thank the reader for the specific question, state what is known and distinguish what remains unconfirmed. Collect no personal information without an appropriate purpose and permission.
pages.question: Does the reply answer the question without inventing an arrangement?

records.label: Availability reply
records.prompt: No actual event or booking is established here.

records.label: Practical enquiry
records.prompt: Price, access and requirements need real confirmation.

records.label: Response boundary
records.prompt: No contact service or reply-time promise supplied.

evidenceRows: 6 planned touchpoints; sequence is not measured behaviour.

pages.title: Define a measure before collecting it.
pages.lead: A real campaign review might examine delivered messages, visits to the outline or practical questions received. Each has a different denominator and interpretation.
pages.body: The six planned touchpoints are not six interactions. No reach, clicks, enquiries or conversions are supplied. Establish a legitimate collection purpose, relevant definitions and appropriate privacy safeguards before measuring.
pages.subheading: Do not turn the map into a funnel report
pages.detail: A later enquiry does not by itself establish which touchpoint caused it. Keep attribution assumptions separate from observed counts.
pages.question: Which observation would tell us whether the explanation was useful?

records.label: Planning count
records.prompt: 6 touchpoints, all planned, none delivered.

records.label: Missing outcome
records.prompt: No observed audience or response data supplied.

records.label: Attribution boundary
records.prompt: Sequence does not establish causation or conversion.

evidenceRows: 6 planned touchpoints; sequence is not measured behaviour.

pages.title: Check the points where trust can break.
pages.lead: A misleading availability claim, inaccessible explanation or unverified image can undermine the campaign before any response is measured. Review the whole path, not only the first asset.
pages.body: Scarcity language and social proof need an actual basis. The template supplies no limited places, endorsements, partner approvals or participant results. Do not add them as decorative persuasion.
pages.detail: Pause if an essential destination does not work, if the operational status is unclear or if the relevant permission is missing. A checklist is not a certification.
pages.question: Which unresolved issue should stop this campaign from being shared?

records.label: Truth check
records.prompt: Concept status remains visible at every touchpoint.

records.label: Access check
records.prompt: The actual explanation and action are accessible.

records.label: Rights check
records.prompt: Distribution and participant permissions are verified.

evidenceRows: 6 planned touchpoints; sequence is not measured behaviour.

pages.title: Close the loop with a useful question.
pages.lead: After an actual campaign, ask which explanation helped people make an informed decision and which practical question kept returning. Keep the review tied to the original purpose.
pages.body: This example contains no delivered activity or results. Its final page is a review method, not a success report. Preserve source versions and distinguish observations from the team’s interpretation.
pages.subheading: A learning loop, not a victory slide
pages.detail: Choose a revision that improves the next explanation. Do not claim that the campaign worked simply because the planned assets were produced.
pages.question: What should change before the next real communication?

records.label: Observe
records.prompt: Record actual delivery and appropriately collected questions.

records.label: Interpret
records.prompt: Separate information gaps from assumptions about demand.

records.label: Revise
records.prompt: Improve the source outline and affected touchpoints.

evidenceRows: 6 planned touchpoints; sequence is not measured behaviour.
